subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should trusted inbound-decoration state become top-level message fields, or live under the existing OpenClaw-owned `__openclaw` metadata bag?
rationale: Both shapes can fix the bug, but the choice establishes a long-lived serialized contract across several packages and determines whether generic message schemas gain new OpenClaw-specific fields.

options.title: Use nested OpenClaw metadata
options.body: Store the canonical bare body under an owned `__openclaw.inboundDecoration` object and update all affected readers to use that single representation.

options.title: Approve top-level fields
options.body: Keep `inboundDecorated` and `bareBody` as additive top-level fields, with explicit maintainer acceptance of the broader persisted-message contract and focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Pause the contract
options.body: Leave the issue and PR open while maintainers define a shared message-metadata policy that this and related plugin-hook work can follow.

recommendation.title: Use nested OpenClaw metadata
recommendation.body: Store the canonical bare body under an owned `__openclaw.inboundDecoration` object and update all affected readers to use that single representation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core persisted-message ownership, compatibility, agents, gateway, memory, and UI rather than one isolated reader.
